newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf ministers fail to agree on unified tariffs.
newsitem.headline: Gulf ministers fail to agree on unified tariffs.

text.p: Ministers from the six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states failed on Sunday to finalise an agreement to unify their customs tariffs, needed to open the door to free trade with other economic blocs.

"We have not reached an agreement on a customs base but we have agreed to prepare a memorandum detailing what has been achieved so far," Oman's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Youssef bin Alawi bin Abdullah told reporters.
Oman chaired the one-day GCC foreign and finance ministers meeting in the Saudi capital Riyadh.
"We have discussed ideas and options which could be adopted at a later stage in order to unify tariffs, achieve a customs union and a free trade region," he added.
The Omani minister declined to give further details.
Differences have been blocking a tariff agreement almost since the formation of the economic and strategic Gulf alliance 15 years ago and a top-level political decision is needed, Arab diplomats say.

GCC and European Union foreign ministers agreed in April to set a deadline of no more than two years to complete a free trade accord between the two trading partners -- an issue under discussion for more than a decade.
But unifying GCC standard tariffs, which vary from four to 12 percent, is among key EU demands for a free trade deal that could open lucrative European markets to cheap petrochemicals from the Gulf.
